items.headline: Wall Street Ends Lower Amid Geopolitical Tensions and Rate Hike Concerns
items.summary: Major U.S. indices concluded the session in negative territory as investors reacted to a stronger-than-expected August jobs report, heightening expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike. Further impacting sentiment were escalating Middle East conflicts driving oil prices to a six-week high and new tariffs in the U.S.-Canada trade dispute. The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) rose by 1.5% to 14.53, reflecting increased market uncertainty.

items.headline: Oracle Surges on AI and Cloud Optimism
items.summary: Oracle Corp ($ORCL) opened up by 4.67% as investors anticipated strong fiscal first-quarter earnings, driven by accelerating demand for Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and AI capacity.

items.headline: FuelCell Energy Sees Strong Intraday Gains
items.summary: FuelCell Energy Inc. ($FCEL) was a notable gainer, up 19.61% in early trading today.

items.headline: Apple Falls as Dow's Major Loser
items.summary: Apple Inc. ($AAPL) was a significant drag on the Dow, with its stock price falling 2.5% today.

items.headline: ServiceNow Leads Software Sector Decline
items.summary: ServiceNow ($NOW) experienced a notable decline, dropping 5.28% as software stocks broadly underperformed.

items.headline: August Jobs Report Fuels Fed Rate Hike Speculation
items.summary: A stronger-than-expected August jobs report, showing an unchanged unemployment rate of 4.1% and a 0.3% increase in average hourly earnings, is increasing investor expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike. The Fed is scheduled to hold its monetary policy meeting next week, with upcoming PPI and CPI data also expected to influence its decision.

items.headline: Oil Prices Surge to Six-Week High Amid Middle East Tensions
items.summary: Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict, sent oil prices climbing to a six-week high. Brent crude rose 1.45% to $99.73 a barrel, while WTI crude was up 1.50% at $94.28 a barrel, raising concerns about potential impacts on global oil supplies and inflation.

items.headline: Canada Implements Retaliatory Tariffs on U.S. Goods
items.summary: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion worth of U.S. goods officially took effect today, escalating trade tensions between the two nations and adding another layer of uncertainty for investors.

items.headline: Sectors Show Mixed Performance; Industrials Lead, Discretionary Lags
items.summary: Today's trading saw mixed sector performance within the S&P 500, with eight of the eleven broad sectors closing in negative territory. The Industrials Select Sector SPDR (XLI) was a notable performer, rising 0.4%. Conversely, Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) fell 1.3%, Health Care Select Sector SPDR (XLV) declined 1%, and Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was down 1%, indicating broad weakness in these areas.

items.headline: United Natural Foods Reports Q4 Results; Other Companies Release Earnings
items.summary: United Natural Foods, Inc. ($UNFI) reported its fourth quarter and full-year fiscal 2026 results before the market open, with Q4 net sales decreasing 0.7% but adjusted EBITDA increasing 48.3%. Other companies, including GameStop ($GME), Braze ($BRZE), and Casey's General ($CASY), were scheduled to report quarterly results today. Philip Morris International also raised its full-year earnings outlook, citing a favorable currency impact.
